en:
Despite Motonari's misgivings, the
Ouchi Army launched a full assault.




But the steep paths to Toda Castle
let only part of the army fight.
The great host counted for nothing,
and time and lives were thrown away.


Meanwhile, the Amago cut the Ouchi
supply lines, and in an instant the
vast Ouchi Army lost the upper hand.
Its very numbers worked against it,
and the tide turned to the Amago.
At this point, the Kikkawa, Mitoya,
Mizawa and others who had defected
to the Ouchi from the Amago went
back to the Amago, and the Ouchi
Army was forced to retreat. Holding
the rearguard were Mouri Motonari
and Kobayakawa Masahira.
The Amago pursuers were already
close on their heels...
